title: India Trail 1-0. Bishnoi's 29-Run Over Still Stings. Trent Bridge on Tuesday Is Do-or-Die.
excerpt: England's shortest boundaries, India's youngest debutant, and a series that threatens to slip away before it's even half done. Here's everything at stake in the 3rd T20I.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India faces a crucial T20I at Trent Bridge, trailing the series 1-0.
  • Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, India's youngest debutant, scored 14 runs in his first match.
  • Ravi Bishnoi's 29-run over was pivotal in India's loss at Old Trafford.
  • Trent Bridge has a history of high-scoring T20I matches, with recent totals above 190.
  • India must improve their death bowling to avoid repeating past mistakes.

Nottingham's Trent Bridge has a reputation. It is the ground where Phil Salt smashed an unbeaten 141 off 60 balls last September. Where 300 was breached in a T20I between Full Member nations for the first time. Where short boundaries and a true surface turn every innings into a potential fireworks display. On Tuesday, it will host the most important match of India's tour so far. ## The Series So Far The first T20I at Chester-le-Street was washed out without a ball bowled. The second at Old Trafford was an instant classic — and India lost it. Shreyas Iyer's side posted 190-7, with Ishan Kishan top-scoring with 49 and Abhishek Sharma blasting 43 off 24 balls at the top. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old who became India's youngest men's international cricketer on debut, contributed 14 in an opening stand of 50. It should have been enough. It wasn't. Arshdeep Singh removed both English openers — Phil Salt and Jos Buttler — for ducks in the first over. At 0-2, India were in dreamland. But Harry Brook counter-attacked with 39 off 15, and when Arshdeep broke the Banton-Bethell partnership, it was Jacob Bethell who took over. The left-hander's unbeaten 76 off 46, including a devastating assault on Ravi Bishnoi's 17th over that went for 29 runs, carried England home with an over to spare. That 29-run over — fuelled by back-foot no-balls from Bishnoi that gave Bethell free hits — is the moment India must exorcise. > **"Bowling coach Morne Morkel spoke before the second T20I about "showing faith and backing the players who delivered a World Cup title." That logic favoured Samson."** ## The Trent Bridge Factor This is not a ground that forgives bowling errors. The last three first-innings totals in T20Is at Trent Bridge were 175, 215, and 232. Four of the 14 men's T20 internationals played here have produced first-innings scores above 190. Seam bowlers can find movement with the new ball under cloudy skies, but once the surface settles, stroke-makers feast. India's plan will need to be more disciplined than at Old Trafford — particularly in the death overs, where Bishnoi and Harshit Rana leaked runs under pressure. Axar Patel was the standout in Manchester, finishing with 1-20 off four overs. His control in the middle overs could be even more critical at Trent Bridge, where spinners must rely on accuracy and variation rather than turn. ![Phil Salt — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4b/2_02_Phil_Salt.jpg) ## Sooryavanshi's Second Chance The big selection question is whether 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi retains his place or makes way for Sanju Samson, the T20 World Cup Player of the Tournament who scored 97*, 89, and 89 in the knockout rounds. Bowling coach Morne Morkel spoke before the second T20I about "showing faith and backing the players who delivered a World Cup title." That logic favoured Samson. But then India picked Sooryavanshi anyway — and the teenager responded with a composed 14 and a spectacular catch in the deep to dismiss Sam Curran.

Kapil Dev praised Sooryavanshi's "raw, explosive talent" while cautioning that "greatness is forged across all versions of the game." Former opener Wasim Jaffer has been more direct, suggesting Samson deserves one more chance. The management must decide: do they back the teenager who has the cricket world buzzing, or turn to the proven performer who won India a World Cup? ## Key Battles **Bethell vs India's death bowlers.** The 22-year-old left-hander dismantled Bishnoi at Old Trafford. India cannot afford a repeat. Varun Chakravarthy's mystery spin could be the answer. **Arshdeep's new-ball threat.** His double-wicket maiden at Old Trafford was electrifying. If he strikes early again, India's middle-overs grip — led by Axar — could squeeze England before the Trent Bridge boundaries come into play. **Brook on his home turf.** The Yorkshire captain smashed 39 off 15 balls in Manchester. At a ground where he has a stunning domestic record, he could be even more dangerous. ## Match Details **When:** Tuesday, July 7 — 5:30 PM local (10:00 PM IST, 12:30 PM ET) **Where:** Trent Bridge, Nottingham **Watch:** JioHotstar (India), Sony Sports Network (TV), Willow TV (US) **Series:** England lead 1-0 (five-match series) India's tour has reached a crossroads. Lose at Trent Bridge and England will take an unassailable 2-0 lead with two matches left. Win, and this series is alive — with the momentum squarely back in India's hands. *Sources: Reuters, ESPN Cricinfo, Cricket Addictor, India Forums*
